title: tune NCCL collectives and KV-cache overlap scheduling for tensor-parallel workloads
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads were showing suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and compute (kernel execution + KV-cache lookups) which increased tail latency and reduced sustained throughput under continuous batching. This PR tunes NCCL stream assignment, introduces more granular stream priorities, adds explicit kernel/collective synchronization points where beneficial, and extends KV-cache scheduling to better pipeline prefix cache warmup with collectives. Goals: 1) improve throughput for TP model shards under continuous batching, 2) reduce p95/p99 latency regressions for short/medium sequences, 3) avoid regressions on single-GPU/local runs.
commits: a1c9f4a: initial tuning pass - adjust stream priorities and add scheduling hooks
b3d2e7c: add async collective helper and priority-aware enqueue path
c4e8f11: integrate KV-cache scheduling to collective orchestration
d9f0a22: unit tests + perf harness + metrics emitted
e2b7c3d: address reviewer feedback (edge cases, fallbacks, docstrings)
review_comments: Ethan Kim: Can you explain the rationale for adding explicit cudaEvent synchronization between the high-priority kernel stream and NCCL stream? We wondered if implicit stream ordering would suffice.

Asha Patel: Explicit cudaEvent sync is added only in the fallback path (heterogeneous kernels) - main fast-path uses eventless priority wiring. Added comments and a small perf test to show the overhead is <1% in fast-path and avoids rare deadlocks.
Priya Rao: Please add a safety knob to disable priority scheduling for older driver/NCCL versions.
Asha Patel: Added a runtime flag (RUNTIME_NCCL_PRIORITY_FALLBACK) guarded by driver query; default remains enabled for CI images with tested NCCL >= 2.19.
Luca Bianchi: Did you run the tp-continuous-batching harness across 2/4/8 GPU shapes? Any regressions on tiny batch sizes?

Asha Patel: Perf results attached in docs/perf/notes-nccl-kvcache-overlap.md; we see 8-12% throughput wins on 4-8 GPU TP with sequence lengths 512-1024 and p99 latency improved 20-35% for common steady-state traffic. Tiny batch regimes (1-2 sequences) see neutral to slightly better p50 but unchanged p99; added conservative fallback for batch<2 to avoid micro-regressions.
release_notes: Performance: tuned NCCL stream scheduling and KV-cache overlap for tensor-parallel workloads. Result: reproducible 8-12% throughput improvement for multi-GPU TP shapes and reduced p99 latency by up to 35% for common steady-state sequences. Includes runtime flag to disable priority scheduling on older drivers.
